content: 1. The absorption of fluoroquinolones, such as ofloxacin, is inhibited by ferrous fumarate in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Ferrous fumarate reduces the levels of mycophenolate by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Mycophenolate decreases the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Patients should avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, patients are advised to consider alternative or additional forms of contraception. 4. Nelfinavir can cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Patients should consider using a non-hormonal contraceptive method. 5. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 6. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, including pills, patches, rings, implants, and progestin-only pills. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Patients should use an effective non-hormonal contraceptive method. 7. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 8. Ferrous fumarate reduces the levels of oxytetracycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 10. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 11. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 12. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 13. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Patients should use an effective non-hormonal contraceptive method. 16. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 17. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 18. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 19. Ritonavir can cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. A non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 21. Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by receptor binding competition. A bolus dose of sugammadex is considered equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives containing estrogen or progestogen. Patients must use an additional non-hormonal contraceptive method (e.g., condoms and spermicides) for the next 7 days. 22. Ferrous fumarate reduces the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Tipranavir can cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. 25. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Amoxicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Ampicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of bendamustine by decreasing its metabolism. Bendamustine is metabolized to minimally active metabolites by CYP1A2. Ethinyl estradiol, a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor, may increase bendamustine plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of bictegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Bictegravir and iron-containing supplements can be taken together with food. However, routine administration of bictegravir under fasting conditions simultaneously with, or 2 hours after, iron supplements is not recommended. 37. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of caffeine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Cephalosporins (e.g., cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, cefuroxime, cephalexin) decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. An additional or alternative form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 40. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Advise women to use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control when using cenobamate with oral contraceptives. 41. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Chloramphenicol decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting GI absorption. Co-administration of ciprofloxacin with multivalent cation-containing products may reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after using these products. 45. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 47. Deferasirox decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting GI absorption. Deferasirox chelates iron. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by weakly inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be diminished. Additional non-hormonal forms of contraception are recommended. 50. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of cyclosporine through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism.
